definitions.explanation: Describes a tendency to focus on internal matters rather than engaging with the outside world. Used for personalities, organizations, or national policies.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{内向|うちむ}きな{性格|せいかく}だ。
{日本|にほん}の{若者|わかもの}が{内向|うちむ}きになっていると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that young people in Japan are becoming more inward-looking.

examples.japanese: {内向|うちむ}きの{政策|せいさく}ばかりでは{国際|こくさい}{競争力|きょうそうりょく}が{落|お}ちる。
examples.english: If we only pursue inward-looking policies, our international competitiveness will decline.

notes:
Used both for personal disposition (introverted, shy) and for broader tendencies in organizations or nations (domestically focused, isolationist). Often contrasted with {外向|そとむ}き.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {内向|うちむ}きな{性格|せいかく}: introverted personality
- {内向|うちむ}きな{姿勢|しせい}: inward-looking stance
- {内向|うちむ}き{志向|しこう}: inward-oriented tendency

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {内向的|ないこうてき}: introverted — specifically for personality; more psychological
- {外向|そとむ}き: outward-looking — the direct opposite
- {消極的|しょうきょくてき}: passive; negative — implies reluctance to act, not necessarily inward focus
